name: who-can-be-bound
of: A mechanism by which a party becomes bindable, so that a promise to or from it can carry weight, named with the hold (what of the party's can be reached, kept, cut, or lost), the carrier that keeps the hold in someone's hand, a market that exists only because of that hold and one that fails without it, the escape from the hold, and how long a stranger needs to acquire it: walked in with, bought at the door, imported from a stay done elsewhere, or accrued only by staying here.
items: Body that can be brought: a party with nothing else is bindable because it can be found, held, and made to appear, so the assetless are bound by custody where the propertied are bound by money, as a fine unpaid becomes a night in jail and a summons ignored becomes a warrant; the bail bond is a market that exists only because a body can be retrieved, since the bondsman prices the recoverability of a body, and no small claim can be brought against a body the court cannot reach; escaped by flight past the reach of whoever must bring it; the hold everyone walks in with, and therefore the hold on the poor.

Kneecap: a party the courts cannot reach is bindable by anyone who can hurt it, so lending to the judgment-proof exists outside the law wherever the lender can reach the borrower's body, as the loan shark and the protection racket lend and insure at rates no court would enforce; not custody, which needs a state to hold the body, but harm, which needs only an asymmetry of force, so it is escaped by acquiring protection or force of one's own, and the market fails the moment the borrower can hit back; walked in with, needing no institution, and for that reason the hold that fills every gap the other holds leave.

Tap: a party becomes bindable the moment it depends on a flow the other side can cut, as the postpaid electricity account, the cloud tenancy, the payment processor, the app store, each of which binds its customer by disconnection rather than by any court; postpaid utility service to strangers exists only because the tap can be shut, and where winter moratoria forbid the cutoff the utility demands a deposit instead; escaped by multi-homing or by becoming too important to cut, as a hospital is; not a license, which a third party revokes to protect others, but a supply the creditor itself withholds, and the one hold a stranger acquires within the hour, by needing.

Deposit at the door: a party posts value into the other's hand before anything is owed, forfeited on breach, as the security deposit, the earnest money, the training bond a new pilot signs, the margin at a clearinghouse; rental housing to strangers exists only because of it, and a stranger with nothing to post is not unbindable but unhoused; escaped by breaching for more than the deposit, since the hold is capped at its amount, and undone by the holder's own temptation to keep it wrongly, which is why a large deposit needs a custodian neither party controls; bought in a day at the price of liquidity, so it is the binding of the newly arrived who have cash and a toll on those who do not.

Ugly hostage: a party hands over a token worth much to it and nothing to the holder, as the car title in a title loan, the diploma a school keeps until fees are paid, the passport an employer holds under kafala, the arrangement Williamson called an ugly hostage; title lending exists only because the paper is useless to the lender and indispensable to the borrower, so the holder is never tempted to keep it wrongly and no custodian is needed, which the same loan against cash could not say; escaped by reissue, since a passport reported lost or a duplicate title unmakes the hold, so it lasts exactly as long as the token cannot be replaced; adjacent to cooperation-ignitions' Hostage before the ask, which is a first move, this is the standing hold and its failure by duplication; handed over in a day.

Rented door: a party becomes bindable on paper by naming a place at which it agrees to be deemed found, so that a summons left there counts as received whether or not anyone read it, as a Delaware company buys a registered agent's address for a small annual fee and a tenant gives an address the landlord can nail a notice to; contracting with an entity nobody will ever visit exists only because it can be served, and a person of no fixed abode cannot rent, bank, or be sued, which leaves them bindable only by body; escaped by letting the door lapse, the agent resigning or the mail returning; not a body, which must be brought, but a place where ignorance can no longer be claimed, bought in a day for the cost of the rent.

Keep the car: the hold arises from the shape of the trade itself when the thing worked on sits in the worker's hands, as the garage keeps the car, the tailor the suit, the innkeeper the luggage, the warehouse the grain, until the bill is paid; repair to strangers exists only because the object can be held, and the same trade on an object that cannot be held, a roof, a field, a hull at sea, fails until statute invents a registered lien on the house in the garage's place; escaped by abandoning the thing when it is worth less than the bill, so a hold on a wreck holds nothing; acquired the moment the thing is handed over, needing no deposit, no court, no name.

Held-back pay: the party is owed a stream the other side has not yet paid, and the unpaid remainder is the hold, as retainage keeps a tenth of every construction invoice until the defects are fixed, the sharecropper's share waits for harvest, the commission waits out the return window; hiring a stranger to build exists only because the last tenth can be withheld, and the prepaid builder who vanishes is the market that fails without it; not a deposit, which is the party's own cash posted before work and costs it liquidity, but the counterparty's money not yet paid, binding from the first invoice and costing nothing up front; escaped in the last period, since a party owed nothing further is bound by nothing further, which is why final payments are disputed and warranties are bonded; acquired by beginning the work.

Someone to sue: a promise can be enforced only against a thing the law recognizes as able to bear an obligation, so a market wanting a side that cannot be bound, a town before incorporation, a club, a protocol without a wrapper, a river, the unborn party to a hundred-year carbon contract, is born only when a proxy is deputized to stand for that side, and the proxy's own holds then govern the market; municipal bonds exist only because a city is a person that can be sued, and a club whose treasurer is personally liable cannot borrow at all; the trading twin of witness-architectures' Deputized injury, which names who may bring a harm, and the two come apart, since a river with a guardian can sue but nobody lends to a river, because no hold reaches the guardian's purse; escaped by dissolving the person or by immunity; bought in a day for a company, never for a river.

Seizable title: a party is bindable through property only if a registry ties the property to its name so that a creditor can find it and take it, as the land registry, the vehicle title, the filed lien; the mortgage exists only because of the registry, and lending against unregistered land fails everywhere the deed cannot be searched, so the same house is collateral in one country and dead weight in the next; escaped by moving the asset past the registry's reach or into an exempt class, the homestead, the pension, the tools; adjacent to survival-floors' Tools the bailiff cannot take, which names the exemptions as a floor, this names what the exemptions are carved from; acquired only by owning something registered, which takes a purchase and a registry, not a day.

Hold at the crossing: a party immune where it stays is bindable through whatever it must send across a border, as a creditor had an Argentine naval training ship detained in a Ghanaian port in 2012, as an airline's aircraft can be repossessed wherever it lands under the Cape Town registry, as a payment in dollars must clear through New York; aircraft leasing to airlines in states whose courts will not enforce exists only because the plane travels, and sovereign lending fails wherever the sovereign keeps everything at home; escaped by not crossing, or by routing through friendly ports; not a seizable title, which sits still under one registry, but a hold that exists only during transit, so the immune are bound exactly as much as they need to move.

Cosigner: a party bound by nothing the creditor can reach borrows the bindability of someone who is, as the parent cosigns the lease, the sponsor signs the affidavit of support, the village group underwrites each member's microloan, the bank issues the letter of credit; renting to a student exists only because of it, and the immigrant with no cosigner meets the deposit instead; the mechanism is an arbitrage of holds, since the guarantor holds on the principal something the creditor lacks, shame, kinship, employment, and sells it priced in the cash the creditor can hold, so it binds only if the guarantor is bindable by another hold on this map and the principal is bindable by the guarantor; escaped when either link fails, the judgment-proof guarantor or the child past shaming; adjacent to exchange-ontologies' Vouching, which names the good, this names the conversion; imported in a day from a stay done elsewhere, by someone else.

Portable file: a stay done elsewhere binds here only if a registry carries its record out, as the credit bureau's file lets a lender bind a stranger it never met, a licensing board's record lets a nurse be hired in a town where nobody knows her, a passport carries a state's vouching across a border; unsecured lending to strangers exists only because of the file, and the credit-invisible newcomer, with a clean past and no record of it, is bound by deposit until a file accrues, as the secured card takes a deposit and returns it once a year of payments has been written; escaped by forging the file, the synthetic identity, or by moving past the registry's reach; not a small world, where the hold is remembered faces, but its export, which loses the face and gains the road; imported in a day from one's own stay elsewhere.

Rent as leash: a party is bound by a revocable permission exactly in proportion to what the permission is worth, so a license binds only through its scarcity, as a medical license is worth more than any single bribe and a taxi medallion at a million dollars bound its owner while the same medallion at a tenth of that bound nobody; surgery by a stranger exists only because the license can be pulled, and the unlicensed trades, the handyman, the mover, run on deposits and small worlds instead; escaped by being the marginal licensee to whom the license is worth little, or by practicing without one; adjacent to cooperation-mechanisms' sunsetting of privileges, which names the sanction, this names the leash's length as the rent, so that a licensor makes its licensees bindable by restricting entry; earned over years, and held by the licensor.

Name worth keeping: a judgment attaches to a name, so a party is bindable through its name only when the name is worth more to it than any single default, as a firm with a brand, a family with a name in the village, a person whose identity is the one thing it cannot replace; the warranty, the prepaid subscription, the long-dated contract exist only because the name will be there to answer, and the gift card from a pop-up fails with the pop-up; escaped by the phoenix, the company dissolved and re-formed under a new name with the old debts left on the corpse, and by the synthetic identity, which is the phoenix for persons; not reputation, which is what a name carries, but the persistence to which anything can attach at all; accrued by staying under one name, which is why a stranger's name binds nothing.

Small world: a party is bindable by memory alone when the set of its future counterparties is small enough that all of them will hear of a default by next week, as the diamond bourses trade parcels on a word and settle disputes by arbitration and expulsion, and, on one historian's reading, the medieval Maghribi traders bound agents across the Mediterranean by a coalition's shared memory; the handshake trade in stones exists only because the world is small, and the same handshake among strangers at a gem show fails, the parcel paid before it leaves the table; escaped by exit, which is why such worlds close their doors, since closure is the binding's carrier and not merely its prejudice; adjacent to cooperation-mechanisms' reputation legible to future partners, this names the bound on the world's size that makes the legibility bind; the denominator is the hold, and it is accrued only by staying long enough to be a face.

Place in line: a party is bound by an ordering it cannot transfer and would lose by leaving, as the pilot's seniority number, the union hall's out-of-work book, the pension that vests at ten years, the founder's equity that vests over four; the airline's investment in a pilot's training exists only because the pilot cannot take the number to another carrier, and the same airline binds the newcomer, whose number is worth nothing yet, by a training bond, a deposit, until the list takes over; escaped only by the institution's own death, since a bankruptcy wipes the list, so the hold is only as good as the institution's name; adjacent to exchange-ontologies' Priority, which names the good, and survival-floors' Hiring hall, which names the floor, this names the hold the institution gets in return; accrued only by staying, and the purest such hold, since the wait itself is the deposit.

source.register: Mechanistic and concrete: bail, retainage, registered agents, title loans, seniority lists, credit files, port seizures; drawn from tenancy, construction, consumer credit, aviation finance, sovereign debt, licensing, and the diamond trade.
source.mode: Analytical distinctions with observed illustrative cases, each simplified to one mechanism; the day-or-stay reading of each hold is an authored simplification, one historical case is marked as contested, and no item is speculative.
source.via: practice-deep-ideonomy; two Fable fieldwork breaths; independent Fable editorial review
boundary_claim: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not an empirical taxonomy or a partition; a real contract usually runs on several of these holds at once, and the list makes no claim to cover every kind.

The seriation is an itinerary by what the party must have done for the hold to exist, not a ranking of strength, legitimacy, or cost; the day-or-stay readings are authored simplifications, since a company is a day and a river never, and map edges are conditional authored claims.

The illustrative cases (bail bonding, title lending, kafala, retainage, the 2012 ship detention, the Cape Town registry, the diamond bourses, pilot seniority, the secured card) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about the full histories; the Maghribi coalition is a contested historical reading and is marked so.

Whether a hold should exist is outside the list; Kneecap and Ugly hostage describe what a cruel hold does to a market's shape, not whether the cruelty is tolerable, and the map does not rank the holds by justice.

cooperation-mechanisms lists several of these holds as bare noun phrases (slashable collateral, hostages, exclusion from vital networks, legible reputation); this map is not a restatement, since its item is the hold with its carrier, its born and failing markets, its escape, and its time-to-acquire, and the walk and edges are what the bare phrases could not show. Holds that live in nobody's hand but the party's own, honor, oath, conscience, are outside, as the boundary case says.

seriation.axis: What the party must have done for the hold to exist: from holds everyone walks in with (a body that can be brought, a body that can be hurt), through holds bought at the door in an hour or a day (dependence on a tap, a deposit, a token handed over, a rented address, a thing left in the worker's hands, work begun), through holds that need an institution outside the two parties (a legal person, a registered title, a border crossed, a guarantor, a file carried out of a stay elsewhere), to holds that accrue only by staying here (a license worth its rent, a name with things attached, a face in a small world, a place in line).
seriation.note: An authored walk, not a scale of strength or a construction order. Body that can be brought opens it because nobody has to do anything for the hold to exist, which is why it is the hold on the poor; Place in line closes it because nothing but time can make it, which is why it is the hold on the loyal. The consequential adjacency is Cosigner → Portable file: both are imports of a stay done elsewhere, the cosigner imports someone else's and the file imports one's own, and the pair teaches that a stranger's day-one bindability is always somebody's staying, exported, so that the registry is the difference between needing a mother and needing a file. Deposit at the door → Ugly hostage is a second lesson, since the two are the same act, handing something over, and differ only in whether the holder could use it. The walk also crosses a second axis twice: the holds that need no institution outside the two parties (body, harm, tap, deposit, hostage, possession, held-back pay, small world, place in line) sit at both ends, and the institutional holds occupy the middle, so that the stranger of a day and the villager of forty years are both bound without courts, and courts bind the party in between, who has stayed long enough to be registered and not long enough to be known.

exploration.first_question: What must be true of a party, in someone else's hands, for a promise to or from it to carry weight, and which market exists only because that hold exists?
exploration.changed_question: Which holds does a stranger walk in with, which can be bought at the door, which are imports of staying done elsewhere, and which accrue only by staying here; and when a hold is escaped, which next hold does the escape recruit? The first breath sorted holds by what is held, an asset, a body, a name; testing the live question against Deposit at the door and Small world showed that the sorting a stranger cares about is time-to-hold, and that holds convert into one another, bail turning custody into cash and the secured card turning cash into a file.

priorities.item: Portable file: a stay done elsewhere binds here only if a registry carries its record out, as the credit bureau's file lets a lender bind a stranger it never met, a licensing board's record lets a nurse be hired in a town where nobody knows her, a passport carries a state's vouching across a border; unsecured lending to strangers exists only because of the file, and the credit-invisible newcomer, with a clean past and no record of it, is bound by deposit until a file accrues, as the secured card takes a deposit and returns it once a year of payments has been written; escaped by forging the file, the synthetic identity, or by moving past the registry's reach; not a small world, where the hold is remembered faces, but its export, which loses the face and gains the road; imported in a day from one's own stay elsewhere.
priorities.why: The passage from a bought hold to an accrued one is where a stranger stops paying tolls and starts being trusted, and it can be checked on paper: an institution either has a rule for converting a deposit into a record and returning the cash, or it does not.
priorities.next_question: Take three holds a stranger buys at the door (a security deposit, a training bond, a secured card's deposit) and find, for each, the institution's written rule for when the record accrued replaces the cash posted and the cash comes back; where no such rule exists, the deposit is a toll rather than a binding, and the operator can predict which newcomers leave.

priorities.item: Someone to sue: a promise can be enforced only against a thing the law recognizes as able to bear an obligation, so a market wanting a side that cannot be bound, a town before incorporation, a club, a protocol without a wrapper, a river, the unborn party to a hundred-year carbon contract, is born only when a proxy is deputized to stand for that side, and the proxy's own holds then govern the market; municipal bonds exist only because a city is a person that can be sued, and a club whose treasurer is personally liable cannot borrow at all; the trading twin of witness-architectures' Deputized injury, which names who may bring a harm, and the two come apart, since a river with a guardian can sue but nobody lends to a river, because no hold reaches the guardian's purse; escaped by dissolving the person or by immunity; bought in a day for a company, never for a river.
priorities.why: Low plausibility that any existing wrapper solves it, high generative promise: every long-dated promise has a side that cannot yet be sued, and the map says such a market runs on the proxy's holds, which nobody has listed.
priorities.next_question: Write the proxy for the unborn side of a hundred-year contract (a trustee, a fund, a guardian) and name, from this map, each hold the living side has on that proxy; then check one existing long-dated instrument, a perpetual trust or a sovereign wealth fund's rule, for which of those holds it actually carries, and whether a market with one bindable side behaves like a market at all.

gate.standard: declared type, close-neighbor discriminator, boundary case, and form inference

neighbors.left: Deposit at the door: a party posts value into the other's hand before anything is owed, forfeited on breach, as the security deposit, the earnest money, the training bond a new pilot signs, the margin at a clearinghouse; rental housing to strangers exists only because of it, and a stranger with nothing to post is not unbindable but unhoused; escaped by breaching for more than the deposit, since the hold is capped at its amount, and undone by the holder's own temptation to keep it wrongly, which is why a large deposit needs a custodian neither party controls; bought in a day at the price of liquidity, so it is the binding of the newly arrived who have cash and a toll on those who do not.
neighbors.right: Held-back pay: the party is owed a stream the other side has not yet paid, and the unpaid remainder is the hold, as retainage keeps a tenth of every construction invoice until the defects are fixed, the sharecropper's share waits for harvest, the commission waits out the return window; hiring a stranger to build exists only because the last tenth can be withheld, and the prepaid builder who vanishes is the market that fails without it; not a deposit, which is the party's own cash posted before work and costs it liquidity, but the counterparty's money not yet paid, binding from the first invoice and costing nothing up front; escaped in the last period, since a party owed nothing further is bound by nothing further, which is why final payments are disputed and warranties are bonded; acquired by beginning the work.
neighbors.separating_case: A contractor with no cash on a job that fails on its first day: retainage holds nothing, since nothing has been invoiced, and a deposit could not have been posted, so the two holds differ in who must have liquidity and in when the hold begins. The same contractor on a job that fails on its last day: the retainage holds the final tenth and the deposit, returned at substantial completion, holds nothing. One is the party's own cash posted before work and capped at its amount; the other is the counterparty's money not yet paid, growing with the work and dying at the last payment.

checks.boundary_case: A man of his word is out: honor binds, but the hold is in nobody's hand but his own, a stranger cannot see it, and no market to strangers has ever been born on it. It enters the map only when the word is spoken before a world small enough to remember it (Small world) or sworn under a penalty that reaches the body (Body that can be brought), and the contract paper itself is out for the same reason, since paper binds only through whichever hold it names.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a loop the sequence conceals: Body that can be brought → Deposit at the door → Portable file → Body that can be brought, where bail converts custody into cash, the secured card converts cash into a file, and know-your-customer sends the forged file back to the body, so that no hold on this map escapes the loop except by staying. It shows a passage between levels at Deposit at the door → Portable file, from a bought hold to an accrued one. It shows a fork at Keep the car → Seizable title, where one trade splits by whether the object can be held into a hold needing no court and a hold needing a registry. It shows an incompatibility at Ugly hostage → Deposit at the door, on the axis of value to the holder, where a pledge cannot be both liquid and untempting. And it shows a dependency at Someone to sue → Seizable title, which splits the whole map into holds that need a court and holds that do not, with the court-free holds at both ends of the walk.
checks.target_preserved: Self-read only. Each item names a distinct hold, a distinct carrier, a market that exists only because of it and one that fails without it, and a distinct escape; the strange members (a hold acquired by needing, a hold worthless to its holder, a hold that exists only in transit, a leash whose length is its rent, a river that can sue but cannot borrow) are kept as mechanisms rather than softened into advice about collateral.
